'''Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami''' (21 May 1945 – 20 July 2015), popularly known as '''Swami''',  was an Indian [[geochemist]] and an honorary scientist at the geosciences division of the [[Physical Research Laboratory]].<ref name="Fellows and Foreign Fellows Deceased during 2015–16">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/INSA_Annual_Report-2015-16_ENGLISH_for_WEB.pdf |title=Fellows and Foreign Fellows Deceased during 2015–16 |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref> He was known for his studies on low temperature geochemistry<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=158 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> and was an elected fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Krishnaswami,_Prof._Sethunathasarma |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N89-1023 |title=Deceased fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=27 April 2017 |archive-date=27 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427194439/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N89-1023 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[The World Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="TWAS fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/member/krishnaswami-sethunathasarma |title=TWAS fellow |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI fellows |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=17 December 2016 |archive-date=6 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[American Geophysical Union]],<ref name="AGU == Biography ==
[[File:P R L.JPG|thumb|235px|left|Physical Research Laboratory]]
Krishnaswami, born on 21 May 1945 in [[Thiruvananthapuram]], in the south Indian state of [[Kerala]], did his graduate studies in science at the [[University College Thiruvananthapuram|University College, Thiruvananthapuram]] of the [[University of Kerala]] and on completion of the degree in 1963, he joined [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] Training School for a short term training.<ref name="Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami (1945–2015)">{{Cite journal |last=Manmohan Sarin |title=Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami (1945–2015) |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/109/05/0984.pdf |journal=Current Science |date=September 2015 |volume=109 |issue=5}}</ref> Subsequently, he joined the geophysics group of [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] as a research associate in 1964 where he stayed till 1972.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> Simultaneously, he enrolled in [[Bombay University]] and secured a PhD in 1974, working under the guidance of [[Devendra Lal]]. His post-doctoral researches were at [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]] with [[Harmon Craig]] and at the laboratory of K. K. Turekian of [[Yale University]]. By this time, he had already moved to [[Physical Research Laboratory]] (PRL), Ahmedabad in 1973 and on returning to India, he spent the rest of his career there, superannuating from service in 2005. He held various positions during his tenure at PRL such as that of a dean from 1987 to 1993 and acting director during 2004–05 and continued his association with the laboratory post-retirement as an [[Indian National Science Academy]] scientist and honorary professor.<ref name="NASI fellows" /> He also served as a visiting scientist at Scripps Institute of Oceanography (1971–72) and as a visiting faculty at the Department of Geology and Geophysics of Yale University for three stints during 1976–77, 1979-1982 and 1986–87.<ref name="Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami (1945–2015)" />

Krishnaswami died on 20 July 2015 at the age of 70, survived by his wife, son and daughter.<ref name="Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami (1945–2015)" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:World geologic provinces.jpg|thumb|235px|The Deccan Traps shown as dark purple spot on the geologic map of India]]
During his research collaborative study at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, Krishnaswami assisted [[Harmon Craig]] in his discovery of ''210Pb-226Ra radioactive disequilibrium in the deep sea''<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> and his association with K. K. Turekian at Yale University helped develop U-Th series nuclide applications in aquatic systems which has been detailed in a book, ''U-Th Series Nuclides in Aquatic Systems'', co-edited by him and published by Elsevier Science in 2008.<ref name="U-Th Series Nuclides in Aquatic Systems">{{Cite book |url=http://store.elsevier.com/U-Th-Series-Nuclides-in-Aquatic-Systems/isbn-9780080450124/ |title=U-Th Series Nuclides in Aquatic Systems |publisher=Elsevier Science |isbn=9780080450124 |editor-last=S. Krishnaswami, J. Kirk Cochran |date=May 2008 |page=440}}</ref> His researches are known to have established the accretion rate and growth history of ocean-floor [[ferromanganese nodules]] which he estimated by [[radionuclide]] method and the work assisted in the determination of the history of sedimentation in Indian lakes and coastal regions.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999}}</ref> He applied these methods in estimating the weathering and erosion in the Himalaya and [[Deccan Traps]] and for assessing their influence on global change.<ref name="Sethunathasarma Krishnaswami (1945–2015)" /> He was also involved in geochemical studies on the rivers of [[Ganges]] and [[Brahmaputra]] for assessing the ''evolution of [[Isotopes of strontium|strontium isotopes]] and uranium concentration in the ocean since the [[Cenozoic era]]''. His studies have been detailed in over 100 peer reviewed articles;{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} the online article repository of the Indian Academy of Sciences has listed several of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Krishnaswami=3ASethunathasarma=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He served as the vice president of [[International Association for the Physical Sciences of the Oceans]] (2003–07)<ref name="Vice President IAPSO">{{Cite web |url=http://iapso.iugg.org/information9/past-executive-committees20.html?showall=&start=3 |title=Vice President IAPSO |date=2016 |publisher=International Association for the Physical Sciences of the Oceans }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> and Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research of the [[International Council for Science]] (1994–96),<ref name="Past SCOR Executive Committee Members">{{Cite web |url=http://www.scor-int.org/SCOR_ExComm_Past.htm |title=Past SCOR Executive Committee Members |date=2016 |publisher=Scientific Committee on Oceanic Research}}</ref> as the treasurer of the [[International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme]],<ref name="IGBP SC Officers and Members">{{Cite web |url=http://www.igbp.net/people/igbpscmembers.4.950c2fa1495db7081e56a.html |title=IGBP SC Officers and Members |date=2016 |publisher=International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme}}</ref> and as a member of the council of the Indian National Science Academy (2002–04).<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> He was also associated with ''[[Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta]]'' and ''[[Journal of Earth System Science]]'' as a member of their editorial boards and mentored 6 doctoral scholars in their studies.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
Krishnaswami received the Young Scientist Medal of the Indian National Science Academy in 1975<ref name="Young Scientist Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php |title=Young Scientist Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=17 December 2016 |archive-date=11 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511084357/https://www.insaindia.res.in/youngmedal.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[Krishnan Medal]] of the [[Indian Geophysical Union]] in 1981.<ref name="Krishnan Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://www.igu.in/awards.htm |title=Krishnan Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Geophysical Union}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1984.<ref name="Earth Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Earth_SCIENCES.htm |title=Earth Sciences |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303200915/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Earth_SCIENCES.htm |archive-date=2016-03-03 }}</ref> He was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies; the Indian Academy of Sciences elected him as a fellow in 1986, followed by Indian National Science Academy in 1989 and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] in 1992. He became a fellow of The World Academy of Sciences with his election in 2000. He was also a fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]],<ref name="AGU fellows" /> [[Geochemical Society]] and [[European Association of Geochemistry]] (2003).<ref name="Geochemical fellows" />
